messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Change the video's camera setup to a rear-view dolly-out shot that moves from upper-body to full-body framing. Use the provided reference image to determine the viewing direction, subject placement, and framing at the start of the edited video. Follow the described camera setup and movement, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video. Retain the same person, hairstyle, hair color, outfit, expression, and action in the same environment. Only change how the camera captures the scene.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Only compare editing requirements; historical appearance words are not observed facts.","original_user_request":"Using the provided source video, apply the following edit: I'd like to change the video's camera setup to a rear-view dolly-out shot that moves from upper-body to full-body framing. Retain the same person, hairstyle, hair color, outfit, expression, and action in the same environment. Only change how the camera captures the scene. Use the provided reference image to determine the viewing direction, subject placement, and framing at the start of the edited video. Follow the camera setup and movement described above, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"She stands on a platform, turns to face the camera, bows deeply with hands clasped, then straightens and turns back to face away.","camera":"Static medium-full shot at eye level, centered on the woman.","clothing":"A sleeveless, knee-length, light-colored patterned dress with a low open back and dark flat shoes.","hair_color":"Dark brown to black.","hairstyle":"Dark hair pulled back into two small buns on top of her head.","identity":"A slender woman with a slim build, seen from behind and then facing the camera.","scene":"A bright indoor transit station platform with an orange 'Exit' sign, a wall clock, and a person bending over in the background."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The output now begins from behind the woman in an upper-body/medium framing near the Exit sign, matching the reference direction and placement. As the clip progresses, the framing widens to show her full body, including dark flat shoes, while she turns, bows, and straightens in the same transit platform environment. The camera appears mostly static or only slightly pulled back rather than a clearly continuous dolly-out, but the requested rear-view and upper-to-full-body progression are present.
arguments.requested_change: Change the camera to a rear-view dolly-out shot starting from upper-body framing and moving to full-body framing, using the reference for initial direction, placement, and framing, while preserving the same person, hairstyle, hair color, outfit, expression, action, environment, and action timing.
uncertain: Whether the subtle camera pull-back qualifies as a dolly-out or is effectively static.
Exact preservation of facial expression is difficult to verify because the subject is mostly seen from behind or in shadow.
unexpected_changes: The output includes a visible double-exposure/ghosting effect in the first frames, which is not present in the source.
The action sequence appears altered: the output shows a bow with clasped hands, whereas the source showed a different forward-leaning/turning motion.
The output framing is closer to a static medium-full shot than a pronounced dolly-out movement.
